title: Invoice validation rules
prompt:
Add `validate_invoice(invoice)` in a new module `app/invoices.py`. `invoice` is a dict. It returns a list of error strings (an empty list means valid), collecting every error in the order of the rules below, and never raises for bad data. Rules:
1. `id` missing or blank -> "missing id".
2. `customer` missing or blank -> "missing customer".
3. `currency` not one of "USD", "EUR", "GBP" -> "unsupported currency".
4. `issued` missing or not an ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD, a real calendar date) -> "bad issue date".
5. `due` missing or not an ISO date -> "bad due date".
6. If both dates are valid and `due` is before `issued` -> "due before issued".
7. `lines` missing or empty -> "no lines".
8. For each line (a dict), numbered from 1, in this order: missing or blank `sku` -> "line N: missing sku"; `qty` not a positive int (bools do not count) -> "line N: bad quantity"; `price` not a number (bools do not count) or negative -> "line N: bad price".
9. Each sku that appears on more than one line is reported once, when its second occurrence is seen -> "duplicate sku: SKU" (these come after all the per-line errors, in the order of those second occurrences). Lines with a missing sku are ignored here.
10. `tax_rate`, if present, must be a number from 0 to 0.5 inclusive -> otherwise "bad tax rate".
11. `total`, if present, must equal round(sum(qty * price) * (1 + tax_rate), 2), where a missing tax_rate counts as 0; only check this when every line is valid and there is no tax rate error -> otherwise "total mismatch".
12. `notes`, if present, longer than 500 characters -> "notes too long".
Add tests in `tests/test_invoices.py`. Run the tests with `python -m pytest -q`, and when they pass commit your work with git.
